title: Georgian forces launch an operation around Tskhinvali on the night of 7-8 August 2008
body:
The Civil.ge chronology records that at 23:35 on 7 August 2008 President Mikheil Saakashvili ordered Georgian forces to stop Russian regular units advancing toward Tskhinvali and to suppress firing positions there. Georgian forces launched manoeuvre operations in the early hours of 8 August and took control of several villages near the South Ossetian capital.

At 02:37 Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Grigory Karasin told his Georgian counterpart, Grigol Vashadze, that Russian forces were starting a military operation in South Ossetia. At about 06:00 Georgian forces advancing from Zemo Nikozi came under fire from the Russian peacekeepers' base, and both sides suffered casualties. Around 11:00 Georgian forces entered Tskhinvali and came under fire from local fighters and Russian aircraft. After 14:00 Georgian officials claimed control of much of the city and announced a pause in fighting from 15:00 to 18:00 so civilians could leave.

Georgian Defence Ministry official Mamuka Kurashvili had said earlier that Georgia had "decided to restore constitutional order", then was reprimanded; he later called his remarks unauthorised and impulsive. At midday Saakashvili called the situation Russian "large-scale military aggression" and announced mobilisation, while Russia's Foreign Ministry accused Georgia of a "treacherous and massive attack". By 20:30 Georgian forces had withdrawn from central Tskhinvali. Which side's fire came first, and when, remains disputed in accounts of the night.
